summary: The investigation could not definitively identify a single root cause; two leading hypotheses—an erroneous validator introduced in the recent auth-service deployment (H1) and a signing‑key configuration change (H2)—remain plausible. Confidence in either is limited by missing observability data and lack of token‑signature evidence. Immediate mitigations and further data collection are recommended.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bug introduced by recent auth-service deployment (JWT library upgrade and validator rewrite)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The deployment of auth-service at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z (dep-5710) included a new JWT library and a rewritten token validator that incorrectly validates incoming JWTs, causing auth-service to return 401 invalid_token for POST /v1/token/validate.

causal_chain.claim: Deployment dep-5710 introduced buggy token validation code
Bug causes valid tokens to be marked invalid

assumptions: The new validator logic misinterprets token signatures or claims
No other service changes affect token validation

ranked_hypotheses.title: Signing key configuration change caused token validation mismatch
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z the signing key config for auth-service was changed from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04. Tokens presented to auth-service were still signed with the old key, so validation failed and auth-service responded with 401 invalid_token.

causal_chain.claim: Signing key config changed to a new key
Incoming tokens are signed with the previous key

assumptions: Token issuance service was not updated to use the new signing key at the same time
Auth-service does not fallback to previous key

ranked_hypotheses.title: Downstream token introspection service failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The token introspection service (token-service) that auth-service calls to validate JWTs became unavailable or returned errors, leading auth-service to treat all tokens as invalid and emit 401 responses.

causal_chain.claim: Token-service experienced an outage or returned errors
Auth-service receives failure response and maps it to invalid_token

assumptions: Auth-service relies on token-service for validation (not just local JWT verification)
Token-service outage coincided with the 401 spike

ranked_hypotheses.title: External identity provider outage or network issue
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external identity provider (kyc-provider) that supplies token signing keys or validates tokens became unreachable, causing auth-service to reject tokens as invalid.

causal_chain.claim: External identity provider experienced outage or connectivity loss
Auth-service cannot retrieve or verify token data

assumptions: Auth-service depends on kyc-provider for token validation or key retrieval

facts.statement: The first 401 invalid_token warning from auth-service was observed at 2026-04-15T14:02:22Z.
CPU usage of auth-service stayed around 38% with no noticeable spike during the incident window.
Request rate of auth-service remained stable around 400 req/s throughout the period.
No 401 warnings were observed in services other than api-gateway, which proxies auth-service.
auth-service was deployed at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z (dep-5710) with a JWT library upgrade and token validator rewrite.
auth-service signing key configuration changed at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04.
No deployments were recorded for user-db between 2026-04-15T13:30:00Z and 2026-04-15T14:30:00Z.
No deployments were recorded for redis-cache between 2026-04-15T13:30:00Z and 2026-04-15T14:30:00Z.

timeline.event: auth-service deployment (dep-5710) with JWT library upgrade and validator rewrite.
Signing key configuration changed from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04.
First 401 invalid_token warning observed on POST /v1/token/validate.
Spike of 401 warnings began (observed via api-gateway logs).
CPU usage measured at ~38%; request rate stable at ~400 req/s.

recommended_actions.action: Revert the signing key configuration to the previous key (k-2025-10) via config change roll‑back.
recommended_actions.rationale: If the 401s are caused by a key‑mismatch (H2), restoring the old key will immediately allow existing tokens to validate.

recommended_actions.action: Rollback auth-service to the version prior to dep-5710.
recommended_actions.rationale: If the new JWT library or validator rewrite is faulty (H1), reverting removes the buggy code and should stop the 401s.

recommended_actions.action: Enable and verify the auth-service log pipeline; ingest logs for the incident window.
recommended_actions.rationale: Access to auth-service logs is required to confirm whether tokens were rejected due to signature mismatch, validator logic, or downstream failures.

recommended_actions.action: Collect missing observability metrics (memory_pct, latency_p99_ms) for auth-service and re‑run the incident window analysis.
recommended_actions.rationale: Missing performance data limits assessment of resource‑related causes.

recommended_actions.action: Query token-service and kyc-provider health/status during the incident period.
recommended_actions.rationale: To confirm or refute hypotheses H3 and H4 regarding downstream dependency failures.

recommended_actions.action: Implement automated tests for JWT library upgrades and coordinated signing‑key rotations, including validation against both old and new keys.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents future deployments or config changes from silently breaking token validation.

recommended_actions.action: Add redundancy to the log pipeline and ensure logs from auth-service are always searchable.
recommended_actions.rationale: Improves observability for rapid root‑cause analysis in future incidents.

data_gaps: Memory usage and latency metrics for auth-service were not retrieved, preventing assessment of performance‑related contributors.
Auth-service logs for the incident window are unavailable due to a log‑pipeline outage, limiting direct evidence of validation failures.
No telemetry or health data for token-service or kyc-provider was collected, leaving downstream dependency status unknown.
No data confirming whether client tokens presented during the incident were signed with the old key (k-2025-10) or the new key (k-2026-04).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that the majority of tokens presented during the spike were signed with the old key (e.g., token logs showing k-2025-10 signatures).
Test results demonstrating that the new validator incorrectly rejects valid JWTs.
Telemetry showing token-service or kyc-provider outages coinciding with the 401 spike.
Successful validation of tokens after reverting the signing key, confirming H2 as the root cause.
